newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA URGES FARMERS TO FORM CREDIT COOPERATIVES.
newsitem.headline: CHINA URGES FARMERS TO FORM CREDIT COOPERATIVES.

text.p: China will promote the transformation of rural credit co-operatives into co-operative financial institutions to curb risk and improve rural financial services, officials said on Monday.

"We must gradually transform rural credit cooperatives into co-operative financial institutions run by farmers who own the shares," the China Securities said, quoting Yin Jieyang, vice president of the People's Bank of China, the central bank.
"We must reduce the financial risk of the rural credit cooperatives to the lowest level," Yin told a working conference on rural financial management, but gave no further details.

However, an official of the agriculture finance management department of the central bank said the converted cooperatives would operate as non-banking financial institutions focusing on providing a service to farmers rather than on making big profits.
Currently, farmers can own shares in cooperatives, pooling their funds to run them jointly, but they can only provide a financial service to their shareholders.
"It will become easier for farmers to obtain loans and will curb high financial risk due to self-management by farmers," he said.
The central bank had taken supervisory responsibility for the cooperatives from the Agricultural Bank of China as part of efforts to sever ties between the cooperatives and commercial banks, he said.
China has 50,000 rural credit cooperatives, non-banking financial institutions that pool credit at the local level and which were set up in the 1950s, another bank official said.
Savings in China's rural credit cooperatives hit 879.4 billion yuan ($106 billion) at the end of 1996.
About 80 percent of loans to rural families and 70 percent of loans to village and township enterprises came from rural credit cooperatives, state media have said.
